1: Evaluation protocol. Images are split by patient into a cross-validation pool and a held-out set. Every choice is made on out-of-fold predictions, and the held-out set is scored once, with patient-bootstrap confidence intervals.
2: Held-out sample-F1 for a frozen DINOv2-S probe, the fine-tuned Swin-T, the best single model and the ensemble. All 95 % confidence intervals overlap.
3: Private leaderboard scores. Our two entries are late submissions and are not ranked.
4: (A) How much a random image-level split and tuning thresholds on the held-out set overstate the score. (B) Mean weight the learned fusion gates give the CNN branch, compared with a fixed average.
5: Change in held-out sample-F1 against the reference Swin-T for each ablation (95 % paired patient-bootstrap interval; p-values on the right). None of the intervals excludes zero.
6: (A) Label efficiency of frozen encoders. (B) Held-out F1 of the frozen probes next to the fine-tuned models.
7: Held-out recall for each class, with patient-bootstrap intervals. The weakest classes are also the rarest.
8: (A) Accuracy on the images the model answers, as a function of coverage. (B) Accuracy targets chosen on out-of-fold predictions, and the accuracy reached on the held-out set.
9: Body-part accuracy on MURA (seven classes), compared with the models reported by Shah et al. (2026).
10: Zero-shot accuracy through the class map, for the softmax and sigmoid heads. Intervals come from an image-level bootstrap and are optimistic.
